title: Fix the Range Filter
statement: Read n, then n integers, then two integers 'low high' on the next line. The program below is supposed to print every number that is strictly between low and high (i.e. low < x < high), space-separated, followed on the next line by how many such numbers there are. It has a few bugs. Fix them so it passes all test cases.
starter_code:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
low, high = map(int, input().split())

result = []
for i in range(1, n):
    if nums[i] > low or nums[i] < high:
        result.append(nums[i])

print(' '.join(map(str, result)))
print(n)
hints: range(1, n) skips the very first element of the list - what range would visit every index?
A number needs to satisfy BOTH 'greater than low' and 'less than high' to be strictly between them - check whether 'or' or 'and' captures that
The count printed at the end should be the size of the filtered result, not the original input size
